Field notes, entry nº 1Virgil Village, Los Angeles

The morning starts
at a window

In Virgil Village, the morning starts at a window. Courage Bagels bakes Montreal-style bagels, wood-fired, blistered and chewy, made to be loaded up and eaten standing on the sidewalk, coffee in the other hand.

There's no dining room, no online checkout, just a queue and a window, and a team with their hands in the work. That simplicity is exactly why the line forms, and why it keeps forming, five mornings a week.

“Difficult to answer our phone, hands full of cream cheese and dough.”

, the owners, in the margin · email is best

How the window works

  • 1 · Join the line

    Head to 777 N Virgil Ave, Thursday through Monday from 7am. On weekends the queue runs 30–40 minutes, it's part of the ritual, and the sidewalk scene is half the fun.

  • 2 · Order at the window

    Walk-up only, every order is taken in person at the window. No online ordering, no delivery apps. Fresh from the wood fire, made while you wait.

  • 3 · Or pre-order by email

    Planning ahead? Write to couragebagels@gmail.com, the surest way to reach a team whose hands are full of dough.

a note on price & patience,

These are premium, made-by-hand bagels: bloggers report them around the $30 mark for a loaded order. And the window runs 7am–2pm only, when they're gone, they're gone.
